title: The Reborn Mummies
summary: Egyptian immortals who die and return, as first shown to the Kindred.

claims.text: A mummy named Sahura was born on the Nile around 2600 BC under Pharaoh Khufu and has died and returned at least 25 times.
Each death and rebirth leaves a mummy a little forgetful, so even a sharp memory cannot hold every past life.
Mummies count Intelligence as memory: at one dot the mind is a sieve, at five it is nearly perfect.

title: The Decline of Egyptian Magic
summary: How mummies remember the fading of the old magic.

claims.text: Sahura recalled the mighty sorcerers of old Egypt, and how magic weakened over the first two thousand years of Sahura's life.
A confusion of theologies muddied the art until it was little more than myth, and the burning of the library of Alexandria added to the loss.
Mummy magic includes necromancy, which in Egypt covered rites to guard the dead on their way, calls to the spirit world and darker workings.

title: Osiris and Set, as Sahura Told It
summary: The mummies' oral account of the war between Osiris and Set.

claims.text: The tale is an oral account full of bias and is surely not true in every detail.
In this account Osiris took blood sacrifices at night, shared blood with an elite guard and made a few of them into the king's image.
Set tore Osiris into pieces and scattered them across the delta, then took Isis and Horus captive.
Set plucked out Horus's eye and trapped Horus's Ba within it.
In the end Osiris was slain and burned completely, and Set left Egypt with Isis and the body of Horus.

title: The Jyhad as Mummies See It
summary: A mummy's view of the Kindred and their war.

claims.text: Horus writes that Camarilla vampires mistake the Jyhad for a petty power struggle in the physical world, blind to its true scope and to the threats facing the realms of the Ba.
